source_name: BQK — Studija: Troškovi plaćanja male vrednosti na Kosovu / Study on the cost of retail payments in Kosovo (Serbian-language edition)
why_relevant: A BQK cost-of-retail-payments study quantifying the social cost of cash versus electronic instruments in Kosovo — the single most directly usable evidence base for cash-usage economics, and it exists in a Serbian-language version confirming BQK's sr publication track.

source_name: BQK/CBK — Card Usage in Kosovo (Përdorimi i kartelave në Kosovë)
why_relevant: The single most on-point document for the card/ATM/POS topics of this cell: dedicated CBK payment-systems analysis of card usage, with ATM vs POS transaction split and growth rates (e.g. domestic POS card payments +30.67% in 2023; POS transactions overtaking ATM as debit cards displace cash for small-value payments). Directly answers card statistics + cash-displacement questions.

source_name: BQK — KosGIRO scheme documentation (legacy direct-debit/bill payment scheme)
why_relevant: KosGIRO is the domestic bill-payment/direct-debit scheme; its documentation names the scheme, participants and transaction types that appear as line items in CBK payment-instrument statistics — necessary vocabulary for parsing the instrument breakdowns.

source_name: BQK — 'Lista e institucioneve financiare të licencuara/regjistruara' (dated PDF list, 22.04.2026 edition)
why_relevant: Machine-harvestable dated snapshot naming every licensed bank, MFI, NBFI, e-money/payment institution, FX bureau and insurer with addresses — the single best seed file for the actor map, and versioned so entries/exits can be tracked over time.

source_name: BQK — 'Use of Bank Cards in Kosovo' / 'Përdorimi i kartelave bankare në Kosovë' annual analytical report
why_relevant: Recurring CBK payment-systems publication dedicated to card issuance (Visa/MasterCard/local share, contactless cards), POS and ATM terminal counts and their geographic concentration — the single richest terminal-level and card-level document series for Kosovo.

source_name: BQK/CBK — Financial Stability Report (Raporti i Stabilitetit Financiar)
why_relevant: Annual analytical report with the richest narrative + tabular view of banking-sector structure, credit growth, NPLs, capitalisation, liquidity, and increasingly payment/digitalisation indicators. Report No. 21 (2025 edition) reports EUR 14.6bn financial-system assets, EUR 6.7bn loans (+14.7% y/y), NPL ~2%. Ideal for sizing and trend context.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore mbi Statistikat e Instrumenteve të Pagesave (Regulation on Payment Instrument Statistics)
why_relevant: The legal instrument that defines exactly which payment-instrument statistics banks must report to the CBK, with reporting templates and frequency. It is the schema key: it tells the collector which series must exist (cards by type, ATM/POS counts, e-banking users) even when the published tables are terse.

source_name: BQK — Register of licensed electronic money issuers (regjistri i emetuesve të parasë elektronike, mandated by the e-money regulation)
why_relevant: The e-money regulation obliges BQK to publish a register of licensed e-money issuers and defines the reporting templates those issuers must file (volumes/values of e-money issued and redeemed). It tells the collector both who must exist in the register and what statistics exist behind it — the request handle for non-bank e-money volume data.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore B15 për autorizimin dhe qeverisjen e IP-ve dhe IPE-ve dhe regjistrimin e AISP (Regulation on authorization and governance of PI and EMI and registration of AISP)
why_relevant: 2026 regulation defining the licence categories (payment institution, e-money institution, account information service provider) that structure the whole non-bank ecosystem. Defines what each category may do and must report — necessary to classify actors correctly and to know which volume statistics are legally collected.

source_name: CBK — Mesečni Statistički Bilten (Serbian-language Monthly Statistical Bulletin)
why_relevant: Serbian-language edition of the same mandated monthly bulletin; resolves the sr language requirement for the A4 cell and provides Serbian statistical terminology for downstream matching. Historic issues (e.g. br. 53, 2006) are archived, giving deep back-series.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për qasjen e ofruesve të shërbimeve të pagesave jo-banka në sistemet e pagesave (non-bank PSP access to payment systems)
why_relevant: Directly governs whether and how non-bank PSPs plug into the national clearing/settlement infrastructure — the structural gate that determines how much card/transfer volume can migrate away from banks. Highest-signal document for forecasting non-bank share growth.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për Sistemin e Pagesave Ndërbankare (interbank payment system regulation, SPN/KIPS)
why_relevant: Defines the national interbank clearing/settlement system (SPN, a.k.a. KIPS — the hybrid clearing+settlement system) — participants, session structure, transaction types. Essential for interpreting KIS/ATS volume series and for naming the actors that generate them.

source_name: BQK/CBK — National Payments Strategy (Strategjia Kombëtare për Pagesat, SKVV)
why_relevant: Strategy documents state baseline and target values for payment-infrastructure indicators (card penetration, POS/ATM density, electronic vs cash share), which both provide data points and reveal what the regulator intends to measure and publish going forward — a leading indicator of future statistical series.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për operacionet me para (Regulation on cash operations, 2023)
why_relevant: Defines the rules banks must follow for cash handling, note fitness/recirculation and authorisation for cash import/export — the regulatory constraint set that shapes the cash-in-transit and cash-management market in Kosovo.

source_name: BQK/CBK — Quarterly Assessment of Macroeconomic Developments (Vlerësimi Tremujor i Zhvillimeve Makroekonomike / VTE)
why_relevant: Quarterly macro assessment giving GDP, consumption, trade and financial-sector context in which payment/card volumes should be normalised. The example found is the Serbian edition, confirming that quarterly output is genuinely trilingual (sq/sr/en) and giving the sr file-naming pattern.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për informacionet e transfereve (Regulation on information accompanying transfers of funds)
why_relevant: Sets the AML/data requirements on every cross-border transfer including MTO remittances; changes here directly alter MTO agent onboarding cost and the friction of cash pay-out, a leading indicator for channel shift from cash to account.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për Instrumentet e Pagesave Elektronike (electronic payment instruments regulation)
why_relevant: Sets conditions for issuing/using electronic payment instruments and the reporting obligations attached to their use — defines the population of card and e-money issuers whose data feeds the card statistics.

source_name: BQK Serbian-language payment-system materials (platni sistem / platni promet)
why_relevant: BQK publishes its payment-system material and annual reports in Serbian as well; this is the Serbian-language entry point covering non-bank payment service providers and clearing volumes, and it also fixes the sr terminology (platne institucije, elektronski novac, platni promet) needed for Serbian-language discovery in this cell.

source_name: BQK — 'Paraja elektronike' consumer brochure (definitions, actor categories, sq/sr)
why_relevant: Supplies the regulator's own local-language glossary for e-money, wallets and non-bank PSPs — the exact Albanian phrasing needed to build reliable sq search queries and to match register entries to trading names.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës / gzk.rks-gov.net
source_name: ASK — Statistical Business Register / Repertori Statistikor i Ndërmarrjeve (monthly)
why_relevant: Monthly statistical repertory of businesses registered with ARBK, plus the RSB covering all public and private enterprises operating in Kosovo. Gives merchant-universe counts by NACE activity, size and municipality — the denominator for POS terminal penetration and acquiring addressable market.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës / gzk.rks-gov.net
source_name: Vjetari Statistikor i Republikës së Kosovës (Statistical Yearbook)
why_relevant: Single consolidated annual compendium containing summary tables from every ASK domain including monetary/financial, ICT, prices and enterprise chapters — the fastest way to establish a baseline year and to spot series that exist but are not exposed in PxWeb.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës / gzk.rks-gov.net
source_name: ASK Annual Report (Raporti Vjetor) series
why_relevant: Describes ASK's full work programme, which surveys ran in which year and which are planned — the authoritative way to know whether ABEF/TIK were fielded in a given year and what new modules (e.g. e-commerce) are coming, rather than inferring from missing releases.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës / gzk.rks-gov.net
source_name: ASK — Niveli i pagave në Kosovë (Wage levels) series
why_relevant: Annual wage-level publication drawing on the Statistical Business Register; wage formalisation and payroll levels are a leading determinant of account ownership and salary-crediting, a core driver of card issuance in Kosovo.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës / gzk.rks-gov.net
source_name: ASK — Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices (HIPC) / Indeksi i Çmimeve të Konsumit, Serbian-language releases
why_relevant: Monthly price series (HIPC base 2015=100, prices collected in 10 municipalities incl. via internet and telephone). Deflator for any nominal payment-value series and an indicator of retail price/channel structure. Confirms ASK publishes the same releases under a full Serbian-language path (/sr/agencija-za-statistiku-kosova/).

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës / gzk.rks-gov.net
source_name: Projektligji për shërbimet e pagesave (draft Law on Payment Services, Office of the Prime Minister)
why_relevant: The forthcoming payment-services law reshapes licence classes, open-banking access and reporting duties for non-bank providers. Legislative pipeline is the earliest leading indicator of new non-bank entrants and of new statistical series becoming public.

source_name: World Bank Group Country Survey — Kosovo 2025 (microdata catalog 8127)
why_relevant: Stakeholder-opinion survey rather than statistics, but useful for identifying which Kosovo institutions and data themes the WB engages with — an actor-map input for the wider source landscape.

source_name: World Bank — Retail Payment Costs and Savings in Kosovo (February 2022)
why_relevant: Kosovo-specific WB cost-of-retail-payments study using PSDG methodology, with primary survey data from households, businesses, 9 commercial banks, CBK, 4 MTOs and the Post — the richest available quantification of cash usage and cash cost in Kosovo.

source_name: World Bank — International mobility as a development strategy: Kosovo Country Report
why_relevant: Country-specific analytical report on Kosovo migration and remittances with source-country structure and channel analysis; a compact, citable baseline for the diaspora-to-cash pipeline.

source_name: World Bank — Monitoring Real-Time Labour Market Trends Through Online Job Vacancies: Kosovo
why_relevant: Methodological pointer that identifies which private Kosovo job portals carry the bulk of online vacancies and how they have been scraped since 2019 — it validates and scopes the job-ad channel this cell depends on, and names the portal universe to cover.

source_name: IMF eLibrary — Kosovo staff country reports and selected issues papers
why_relevant: Structured HTML/XML access to Kosovo staff reports and selected-issues chapters (e.g. 'Using Digitalization to Enhance Public Finance in Kosovo'), easier to parse than PDFs and useful for topic-level retrieval on digital payments.

source_name: IMF Article IV / Stand-By & RSF staff reports and technical assistance reports on Kosovo
why_relevant: Staff reports carry standardised statistical annexes built on CBK data plus an explicit assessment of data quality — the FSSR/TA reports evaluate how the CBK compiles financial soundness indicators, monetary and financial statistics and balance-sheet matrices. That is the best independent read on how much to trust each CBK series, and it flags known gaps.

source_name: IMF FAS Annual Report (latest edition PDF)
why_relevant: Narrative + methodology companion to the FAS dataset; documents definitions (what counts as a POS terminal), coverage changes and reporting quality — essential for interpreting Kosovo series breaks.

entity_name: Bank tariff/price-list disclosures surfaced via Albanian media and search
source_name: BKT Kosova — audited IFRS financial statements PDFs
why_relevant: Full audited IFRS statements with notes for BKT Kosova (incl. BKT Pay subsidiary), the layer where fee/commission income from cards and payment services can be isolated per institution.

source_name: EBRD — Transition Report country assessments: Kosovo
why_relevant: European multilateral bank producing an annual Kosovo assessment that has explicitly covered the CBK National Retail Payments Strategy 2021-26, cashless-payments-per-capita and account-ownership objectives, and Kosovo's cash-transaction restrictions. One of the few European institutional sources with concrete retail-payment policy detail on Kosovo.

source_name: EEAS — EU Office in Kosovo / EUSR: SAA Sub-committee on Economic and Financial Issues and Statistics conclusions
why_relevant: Treaty-based bilateral body (SAA) that meets roughly annually and whose published conclusions record the EU's specific statistical and financial-sector asks of Kosovo — including statistics production and financial-sector supervision. Conclusions are also posted by the Ministry of European Integration, giving a local-language mirror.

source_name: Kosovo media coverage of ASK releases (kallxo.com, teve1.info, info-ks.net)
why_relevant: Local outlets report ASK headline numbers within hours of publication and often quote figures before the PDF is indexed; useful as a low-cost change-detection tripwire for ABEF/TIK/HIPC releases and for the Serbian-language read (info-ks.net tags 'Agencija za statistiku Kosova').

source_name: European Commission (DG NEAR) news — SEPA inclusion statements for Western Balkans partners
why_relevant: Commission communications that document the political/legal conditionality behind SEPA inclusion in the region — the template Kosovo must satisfy (payment services law alignment, AML framework, PSP supervision). Useful as an early-warning feed for a Kosovo announcement.

source_name: ProCredit Holding AG — Annual Report (group), Kosovo subsidiary key-figures table
why_relevant: Frankfurt-listed parent publishes a per-country key-figures table (loan portfolio, portfolio growth, defaulted-loan share, staff) with an explicit Kosovo row, plus group commentary on digital/direct banking rollout in Kosovo.

source_name: RBI Semi-Annual / Quarterly Financial Report — country analysis incl. Kosovo
why_relevant: Search snippet indicates an explicit Kosovo column in the segment/country analysis (net interest income, net fee and commission income, operating result), giving semi-annual Kosovo market data with fee income as a proxy for payments/card activity.

source_name: BKT Albania (parent) — consolidated periodic financial reporting incl. Kosovo
why_relevant: BKT Albania's consolidated periodic reports explicitly consolidate 'the Bank, its branch in Kosovo, and BKT Pay', and are published quarterly — a higher-frequency read on the BKT Kosovo perimeter than the Kosovo entity's annual report, and reachable when bkt-ks.com blocks our fetcher.

source_name: TEB Sh.A. Kosovo — Annual Report PDFs
why_relevant: Verified content-rich: the 2024 report contains a 'Card and POS Business' section, an explicit 'POS Terminals 5,593 Total' figure, and branch expansion ('opened 4 new branches, bringing the total number to 34, up from 30 in 2023'), plus sector commentary (e-banking accounts >1 million, POS transactions +32%). This is exactly the per-institution ATM/POS/card granularity the cell targets.

source_name: Council of Europe — PECK II project: Assessment report on Kosovo's compliance with international AML/CFT standards (FATF/MONEYVAL methodology)
why_relevant: The functional substitute for a MONEYVAL mutual evaluation, since Kosovo is not a Council of Europe member and therefore not a MONEYVAL member. Applies FATF/MONEYVAL methodology and is the main European assessment discussing Kosovo's cash-intensive economy, cash-transaction thresholds, non-bank money transfer and AML controls on cash.

source_name: ECB — publications on official euroisation/dollarisation and the international role of the euro (ECB Occasional Paper No. 11 and successors)
why_relevant: The ECB's institutional position on unilateral euroisation — the framing that determines why Kosovo gets no euro-area cash-issuance data, no direct ECB payment statistics coverage, and no Eurosystem cash-cycle reporting. Essential for correctly caveating any euro-cash-in-Kosovo estimate.

source_name: IOM Kosovo — diaspora and remittances programme publications
why_relevant: IOM's Kosovo mission publishes diaspora-engagement analysis citing remittance shares of GDP and household receipt rates; useful for triangulating household penetration of remittances (share of families receiving) which maps to cash-withdrawal behaviour.

source_name: Narodna banka Srbije — saopštenja o dinaru na Kosovu i Metohiji
why_relevant: NBS press/Q&A items are the issuing authority's own account of the ban on dinar cash entry into Kosovo, cash-transport arrangements (Leposavić treasury, Jarinje crossing, licensed CIT carrier), and volumes/purposes of dinar funds sent for salaries, pensions and social benefits. Primary institutional commentary on parallel cash channels.

entity_name: Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo historic annual reports mirrored on Yumpu
source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo historic annual reports mirrored on Yumpu
why_relevant: Third-party mirror of older Raiffeisen Kosovo annual reports that are no longer linked from the bank's current site — valuable for building long time series on card/ATM/POS counts back through the 2010s.

entity_name: Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo historic annual reports mirrored on Yumpu
source_name: Yumpu-hosted historic Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo annual reports
why_relevant: Third-party mirror of older RBKO annual reports; a fallback for pre-2010 or delisted years that the bank's own archive no longer serves.

source_name: Academic article: 'Determinants Affecting Consumer Acceptance and Adoption of Internet Banking in Developing Countries: the case of Kosovo' (Economic Studies / Ikonomicheski Izsledvania)
why_relevant: Kosovo-specific survey on e-banking adoption determinants; useful for adoption-barrier framing and for identifying the Kosovo academic authors who repeatedly field payment-behaviour surveys.

source_name: Ziraat Bankası — Entegre Faaliyet Raporu (integrated annual report), international/Kosovo branch network sections
why_relevant: Ziraat operates in Kosovo via a country management office and branches (Prishtinë, Prizren, Pejë, Ferizaj); the integrated report's international-network chapter is the main public account of that presence and its branch/service footprint.

source_name: UNDP Kosovo — Kosovo Diaspora reports and Kosovo Remittance Studies
why_relevant: UNDP's Kosovo Remittance Study series (with BQK, ASK, IMF, USAID involvement) is the main survey evidence on HOW remittances arrive — notably that cash carried in person during family visits dominates over formal channels. This informal cash channel is invisible in banking statistics yet is a major driver of physical cash circulation.

source_name: Academic article: 'Switching from Cash to Cashless Payments: Consumer Behavior Evidence from Kosovo' (Zeqiri et al., JLIA)
why_relevant: Original consumer survey measuring drivers of the cash-to-cashless switch in Kosovo, with an explicit instrument and sample — exactly the kind of demand-side evidence absent from official payment statistics. Authors are a traceable Kosovo academic cluster to snowball on.

source_name: Banka për Biznes (BPB) — Raporti Vjetor & audited statements
why_relevant: BPB posts Albanian-language annual reports and independent auditor reports back to at least 2016 on its WordPress uploads tree; a mid-size domestic bank whose card/POS acquiring scale is otherwise invisible.

source_name: Compass Plus Technologies — customer success stories and newsroom (Quipu / Kosovo processing centre)
why_relevant: Compass Plus publishes a documented Kosovo deployment: Quipu's Kosovo card processing and personalisation centre running the TranzWare suite since 2004, with hard issuance numbers (6,000 contactless cards in under a month, 20,000 target). This is exactly the vendor-side quantification of Kosovo card infrastructure that precedes official statistics.

source_name: diasporafordevelopment.eu — Kosovo country factsheet (EU/ICMPD diaspora programme)
why_relevant: Compact EU-funded factsheet with emigration stock and remittance-to-GDP indicators for Kosovo; convenient pre-aggregated cross-check and a pointer to the wider EU diaspora-programme document set.

source_name: EBRD Trade Facilitation Programme awards — 'Most Active Issuing Bank in Kosovo'
why_relevant: An IFI-issued, volume-based award (NLB Banka Prishtina repeatedly named most active issuing bank in Kosovo) — a rare externally validated ranking of trade-finance/payment activity by institution.

source_name: European Parliament — annual resolution and AFET report on the Commission reports on Kosovo
why_relevant: Parliamentary scrutiny layer that restates and sometimes sharpens Commission findings on Kosovo's economy, informality and EU financial integration; useful for detecting which financial-sector issues are politically salient and for citations to underlying data.

source_name: German Economic Team — analysis of Kosovo's SEPA accession process (EU-adjacent advisory, non-official)
why_relevant: One of the few dedicated analyses of the two-step Kosovo SEPA accession mechanism (country inclusion in geographical scope, then PSP scheme adherence) and the legislative prerequisites for the Ministry of Finance and CBK. Useful as a pointer to the underlying EPC/EC criteria; not an official source and should be corroborated.

source_name: Halcom d.d. — e-banking vendor with declared Kosovo market entry
why_relevant: Halcom's corporate history states it won Kosovo and Albania as new markets and that Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo was the first user of its mobile bank — a dated, named Kosovo customer reference identifying the vendor behind a major Kosovo bank's digital channel.

source_name: IFC — Kosovo digital financial services programme (IFC/SECO with CBK)
why_relevant: Signals an active IFC/SECO advisory programme with CBK on payment-services law, open banking and digital finance — such programmes typically generate diagnostics, market assessments and workshop data on Kosovo payments; a lead-generator for future primary documents.

source_name: Javni servis (javniservis.net) — long-form Serbian analysis
why_relevant: Serbian-language analytical/long-form outlet carrying essayistic treatment of the dinar removal and its social-payments consequences. Lower authority but useful for framing, actor names and the lived mechanics of parallel payment channels.

source_name: NLB Group quarterly results presentations (nlb.si financial-reports PDF tree)
why_relevant: Results decks carry per-market slides with Kosovo market share (loans/deposits), client counts and digital-channel adoption metrics — the closest thing to a published Kosovo digital-payments KPI series from a private issuer.

source_name: NLB Komercijalna banka — Kosovska Mitrovica branch network (Serbian-serving retail)
why_relevant: Pointer to the commercial-bank layer serving Serbian clients: reporting describes a Kosovska Mitrovica branch with multiple outposts across Kosovo and Metohija, a five-figure client base, and dual-currency ATM withdrawal — a rare concrete datapoint on ATM currency configuration in Serbian-majority areas. Use as a lead into the bank's own disclosures and CBK licensing records rather than as an authority itself.

source_name: OneFor (OneFor Holding GmbH) — licensed non-bank financial institution in Kosovo, eWallet + Mastercard
why_relevant: Diaspora-focused digital wallet + Mastercard issuer licensed by BQK as an IFJB; a founding member of the FIKS fintech cluster. Card issuance by a non-bank is exactly the activity this cell must track, and its Albanian-language launch coverage carries product and volume claims.

source_name: Quipu GmbH (ProCredit group) — card processing and personalisation centre operating in Kosovo
why_relevant: The clearest documented non-bank card processor/personalisation centre with Kosovo operations, running issuing and acquiring on the TranzWare (Compass Plus) switch. Its press disclosures carry hard operational numbers (cards issued, ATMs, POS terminals, monthly transaction counts) — rare processor-side statistics for this market.

source_name: SIGAL Kosovë — Sigurimet Financiare / 'Sigurimi i Bankave' (bank and cash-in-transit insurance product page)
why_relevant: Insurer product page covering cash-in-safe and cash-in-transit cover for banks in Kosovo. Insurance product structure and the existence of a dedicated bank/CIT line is an indirect reveal that a commercial cash-transport market exists and of the risk categories it is priced on — one of the few open windows on a sector with no public operator data.

source_name: Swinto (Velanis AG) — Switzerland–Kosovo remittance and payments platform
why_relevant: Non-bank remittance/payments app targeting the Swiss-Kosovar diaspora corridor, FIKS founding member. Remittance corridors are a major driver of cash-in/cash-out and card loads in Kosovo; partner announcements (Currencycloud) reveal rails and sometimes corridor volumes.
